articles.summary:
Alibaba is raising HK$80 billion, approximately $10.2 billion, through a record-breaking share placement in Hong Kong to aggressively fund its expanding artificial intelligence infrastructure and compute capabilities.

### Key Points
- The share placement marks the largest primary follow-on offering ever conducted by a Hong Kong-listed company.
- Alibaba reported a 75% decline in quarterly net profit as capital expenditure surged to 67.68 billion yuan.
- Revenue from cloud and AI services grew by 45% to 48.44 billion yuan during the most recent quarter.
- CEO Eddie Wu plans to increase the company's three-year investment commitment from 380 billion yuan to 480 billion yuan.
- The company is expanding its European presence with new availability zones in Paris, Germany, and Britain.

### Why it Matters
This massive capital injection highlights the intense global competition to secure AI compute capacity, with Alibaba’s single offering rivaling the scale of entire regional government programs. While the company seeks to capture international market share, its expansion faces potential regulatory friction from European sovereignty frameworks that favor locally owned cloud providers.

articles.title: The Asus Googlebook is reportedly going to cost ~$1,400, spelling the end for its affordable range
articles.author: Simon Batt
articles.content:
Summary
- Several months ago, Google revealed a new brand of laptops called the Googlebook.
- A leaked Asus listing prices a Googlebook at ~CA$1,900 (~US$1,400), hinting at pricier hardware.
- Specs like Core Ultra 5, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD back a higher price, but leaks may show placeholders.
A little while ago, Google confirmed it planned to place less of an emphasis on its affordable range of Chrome OS-powered Chromebooks. The goal was to pivot more toward on-board AI processing with a new brand of laptops called Googlebooks. At the time, it sounded like Google no longer wanted to support the budget-friendly range, but we didn't know just how budget-unfriendly Googlebooks would be.
Well, if a leaked price is to be believed, we're looking at laptops priced around $1,400.
A leaked Asus Googlebook price pins it at ~$1,900 Canadian
That's around $1,400 American
As spotted by VideoCardz, a new laptop has appeared on the PC-Canada retailer's website. It's listed as the "Asus Nb Cx9406caa-dsu51t-cb," which likely correlates to the Asus Googlebook CX9406 we know is on the way. The website lists the price at around $1,900 in Canadian dollars; that comes to around $1,400 when converted to US dollars.
Looking at the specs in the product title, it's easy to see why. We're looking at an Intel Core Ultra 5 Processor 325, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of space, presumably on an SSD. If true, it shows that Google is no longer interested in supplying people with a hardware-light laptop for budget purposes; this laptop is designed to be more of a powerhouse than its older cousin.
As is the case with leaks like these, take the price with a grain of salt. Websites like this will sometimes post placeholder prices before they receive news on how much it will actually cost. However, given the specs, it doesn't seem too unrealistic to price it in the low-to-mid $1,000 range.
articles.summary:
A leaked retail listing for the upcoming Asus Googlebook suggests a premium price point of approximately $1,400, signaling Google's strategic shift toward high-performance, AI-capable hardware over budget devices.

### Key Points
- A PC-Canada listing identifies the Asus Googlebook model CX9406 with a price tag of roughly CA$1,900, or US$1,400.
- The hardware specifications include an Intel Core Ultra 5 Processor 325, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD.
- Google is pivoting its laptop strategy away from affordable, entry-level Chromebooks to focus on devices capable of advanced on-board AI processing.
- Industry analysts note that retail listings often use placeholder pricing, though the high-end specifications align with a premium market positioning.

### Why it Matters
This pricing strategy confirms Google's intent to compete in the premium laptop market rather than maintaining its traditional dominance in the budget-friendly education and entry-level sectors. By prioritizing high-performance hardware, the company aims to support intensive on-board AI tasks that standard, low-cost Chromebooks cannot handle.

articles.title: Here’s what people who have used the iPhone Ultra like most
articles.author: Chance Miller
articles.content:
We’re just a few weeks away from the rumored launch of the foldable iPhone Ultra. As we’ve written before, excitement for the device is mounting.
A new report from Bloomberg today outlines what people inside Apple who have used the iPhone Ultra love about it.
iPhone Ultra is coming: Real-world impressions
In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman offers a detailed recap of the foldable iPhone. In particular, he says he has “spoken to several people” who have used the device. Those people say they like these things in particular:
- How well it fits in a pocket. Rumors say it has a 5.5-inch outer display.
- The durability of the hinge.
- The new “iPad-like app layouts” that take full advantage of the inner display, which reports suggest measures around 7.8 inches and is wider than it is tall.
- How well it serves as a “camera viewfinder.”
Multiple reports suggest the iPhone Ultra will cost upwards of $2,000. It’s expected to have a main camera and an ultra-wide camera, but not a telephoto camera. It will reportedly use Touch ID instead of Face ID for biometric authentication.
9to5Mac’s Take
I’m incredibly excited for iPhone Ultra, and these tidbits from Gurman only make me even more optimistic it’s the device for me.
I was originally skeptical of the foldable iPhone’s form factor. However, as we’ve learned more about the specific size and its benefits, I’ve come around to it.
The positive reviews of Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 have also offered great real-world insight into a very similar form factor to the iPhone Ultra.
There will, of course, be limitations compared to the iPhone 18 Pro. I use an iPhone Air right now, so I’m used to life without a telephoto camera, and a return to Touch ID doesn’t seem like much of an adjustment.

Apple is reportedly preparing to launch the foldable iPhone Ultra, a new device featuring a 7.8-inch inner display and a compact design that has impressed early internal testers.

### Key Points
- The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature a 5.5-inch outer display and a 7.8-inch foldable inner screen with iPad-like app layouts.
- Early reports highlight the device's pocket-friendly form factor, durable hinge mechanism, and utility as a camera viewfinder.
- The device will reportedly utilize Touch ID for biometric authentication rather than the Face ID technology found on standard iPhone models.
- Hardware specifications include a main camera and an ultra-wide lens, with an anticipated retail price starting at approximately $2,000.

### Why it Matters
This device represents Apple’s first major entry into the competitive foldable smartphone market currently dominated by competitors like Samsung. If successful, the iPhone Ultra could establish a new premium category for the company and influence future mobile hardware design standards.
